<p class="mkt-lead">A blog post, a slide deck, a book, and a website are the same document seen four ways. They share the block model, the offline math and highlighting, and the live edit loop — so anything you learn for one carries to the rest.</p>

::: {.mkt-section-head}
<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Article</span>

## Blog posts & papers {#blog-posts}

The default output. Prose with everything a technical piece actually needs.
:::

Write Markdown and get a clean reading column with web-native typography. Add
display and inline math, mermaid diagrams, numbered figures, callouts, and
`[@key]` citations with a real bibliography. Drop in `{python}` or `{r}` cells and
their output, including matplotlib figures, renders inline and re-runs only when
the code changes.

```yaml
---
title: "A post about something hard"
bibliography: references.bib
---
```

Live Observable inputs and Three.js scenes belong here too: they keep their
runtime state while you edit the prose around them.

::: {.mkt-section-head}
<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Reveal</span>

## Slide decks {#slide-decks}

`format: revealjs` turns the same headings into a deck, on qmd-fast's own engine, with no reveal.js dependency.
:::

Fragments and incremental lists, a presenter view with notes and a timer,
one-slide-per-page PDF export, per-slide backgrounds, auto-animate, magic-move
code, and step-through line highlighting. And because the exec pipeline is
format-agnostic, a `{python}` cell **runs on the slide** and re-runs as you edit it.

{{< embed demo.qmd title="The qmd-fast deck engine" >}}

The deck above is live — click it, arrow through it, press <kbd>F</kbd> for fullscreen.

::: {.mkt-section-head}
<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Book</span>

## Multi-chapter books {#books}

A `chapters:` list makes a book: a sidebar, numbered chapters, cross-chapter references.
:::

References like `@fig-` and `@sec-` resolve and number across chapters, a Cmd-K
palette searches the whole book, and each chapter is still a normal `.qmd` you can
preview on its own.

::: {.mkt-cta}
[Read the docs — they are a qmd-fast book](docs/){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

::: {.mkt-section-head}
<span class="mkt-eyebrow">Site</span>

## Multi-page websites {#websites}

Point qmd-fast at a directory with a `_quarto.yml` and you get a whole site.
:::

A themed navbar and footer, post listings and an `about:` profile header, an RSS
feed, OpenGraph and Twitter-card metadata, light/dark with a toggle, and Cmd-K
search — built to a static `_site/` you can host anywhere. Intra-site `.qmd` links
are rewritten to `.html` automatically.

::: {.mkt-dogfood}
This site is the example. The page you are reading, its navbar and footer, and the
dark/light toggle are all a qmd-fast website — and the [docs](docs/) it links to are
a qmd-fast book, deployed in the same tree under `/docs`.
:::
